body:
_**This PR introduces full internationalization (i18n) support across the app:**_

**Locale Files**
Extracted all UI strings into separate en.js and ua.js under utils/i18n/locales/
Centralized translations in utils/i18n/index.js using i18next and react-i18next

**Language Detection & Fallback**
Automatically picks up device language via expo-localization
Falls back to English if the locale isn’t supported

**Component Integration**
Wrapped the app entry point to initialize i18n before rendering (import './utils/i18n';)
Updated MoodPicker, navigation labels, buttons, etc. to use the t('key') lookup

**Ready for Expansion**
Easily add new languages by dropping in additional locale files
Components remain clean—no hard-coded strings

# Summary of Git Diff

This Git diff shows updates made to several Java files in a project related to the deletion of audio data. The primary changes include the introduction of a method to clear the entity manager cache, refactoring of method signatures to remove unnecessary parameters, and modifications to unit tests to accommodate these changes.

## Highlights

- **Added `clearEntityManagerCache()` Method**: 
  - Introduced in `TestBase.java` to manage entity manager states effectively.
  
- **Refactoring of Method Signatures**:
  - Removed the `UserAccountEntity` parameter from methods like `markForDeletion` and `markMediaRequestAsExpired` in `OutboundAudioDeleterProcessorSingleElement.java` and its implementation.
  
- **Changes in Test Cases**:
  - Updated test cases in `OutboundAudioDeleterProcessorTest.java` to call `clearEntityManagerCache()` before assertions to ensure a clean state.
  
- **Removal of UserIdentity Dependency**:
  - The `UserIdentity` dependency was removed from `OutboundAudioDeleterProcessorImpl`, leading to a streamlined approach in handling media requests.

- **Minor Code Adjustments**:
  - Various methods were adjusted to reflect the new method signatures and to ensure consistency across the implementation.

These changes improve code readability, maintainability, and the overall functionality of the audio deletion process within the application.

author: ambienttea
body:
# Description

I'm leaving this PR as draft to first have a discussion if this is something we want.

* Moves logic wiring data sources and RPCs out of our demo node into a new `partner-chains-node` crate. This crate provides:
    - `PartnerChainDataSource` - a wrapper around all our data sources and time source
    - `PartnerChainNodeConfig` - wraps the configuration that we read from environment + makes the logic to read it accessible to users
    - `partner_chain_rpc!` - macro that adds our RPCs into the rpc module. accepts the data source + config and hides the wiring inside
  The crate provides data source and RPC for the sidechain and mc-hash functionality, and hides the rest behind feature flags. The idea is that after this crate is wired into the node, enabling a new feature should more or less work out of the box without additional integration by the node developer
* Removes the "unit tests" from the demo node. These tests weren't really useful and forced us to expose mocks from other crates to implement them, and forces the node to depend on internal data sources.

Unfortunately feature flags can't be applied to bounds in `where` clauses, which means that it's not possible to define helper traits that would free the node from needing to specify exactly which runtime Apis etc. are needed from each type, ie. I couldn't get this to work:
```
fn create_rpc<C>(..)
where
    #[cfg(feature = "block-participation")]
    C: BlockParticipationApi
    #[cfg(feature = "governed-map")]
    C: GovernedMapApi
{...}
```

# Checklist

- [ ] Commit sequence broadly makes sense and commits have useful messages.
- [ ] The size limit of 400 LOC isn't needlessly exceeded

It was was developed within the framework of Architecture of Integrated Information Systems (ARIS) by August-Wilhelm Scheer at the Institut für Wirtschaftsinformatik, Universität des Saarlandes (Institute for Business Information Systems at the University of Saarland) in the early 1990s.

Submitted by @chh1107

Items: Association, Information Flow, Control Flow, Supporting System, Organization Unit, Information Object, XOR, OR, AND, Function, Event

author: aruggero
body:
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SOLR-17760

# Description

A bug in the LTR dense/sparse format has been fixed with this PR. 
Dense/sparse format was not working for some features (e.g. FieldValueFeature) since default values were returned in the sparse format.
A check if the scored feature has the default value has been added. If it is, the value is excluded from logging in the sparse format.

# Solution

The `if (featuresInfo[featureId].getValue() != scFW.getDefaultValue())` condition has been added in both the `org.apache.solr.ltr.LTRScoringQuery.ModelWeight.ModelScorer.SparseModelScorer#score` method of the SparseModelScorer and in the `org.apache.solr.ltr.LTRScoringQuery.ModelWeight.ModelScorer.DenseModelScorer#score` method of the DenseModelScorer in the [LTRScoringQuery](https://github.com/apache/solr/blob/main/solr/modules/ltr/src/java/org/apache/solr/ltr/LTRScoringQuery.java) class.

Also, the `isUsed` variable of the org.apache.solr.ltr.LTRScoringQuery.FeatureInfo class has been renamed to `isDefaultValue` for more clarity.

Finally, the documentation has been updated, integrating the `defaultValue` parameter, which is a parameter supported by all the LTR features but was not present and explained in the reference guide.

# Tests

[TestSelectiveWeightCreation](https://github.com/apache/solr/blob/main/solr/modules/ltr/src/test/org/apache/solr/ltr/TestSelectiveWeightCreation.java) and [TestFieldValueFeature](https://github.com/apache/solr/blob/main/solr/modules/ltr/src/test/org/apache/solr/ltr/feature/TestFieldValueFeature.java) have been adapted to reflect the fixed behaviour.

author: coffeefuelled
body:
Currently the income multiplier (advantage/bonus) applies to reclaim (unit reclaim and feature reclaim). This may or may not be desirable to game developers. However, when it is not desirable it becomes game breaking (for example by reclaiming more resources than used to create a unit).

While this touches upon the realm of game design, this PR proposes changing the default behaviour provided by the engine to one of not applying the income multiplier to reclaim.

As far as I can see, there are currently no options provided to select alternative income multiplier behaviours .

A more comprehensive solution moving forward may be to provide options to game devs to select what the income multiplier is applied to.


Note: I haven't added the new variable in SResourceOrder to CREG. Does it need to be? The whole struct is only used temporarily.

edit: closes #2270

author: tckarenchiang
body:
## What is the current behavior?
When running the alphamini demo, the following error occurs,

```
[09:03:59] [AlphaminiDeviceManager 192.168.178.84]------DEBUG: SSH command exited with status: 1
[09:03:59] [AlphaminiDeviceManager 192.168.178.84]------DEBUG: SSH command output: 
[09:03:59] [AlphaminiDeviceManager 192.168.178.84]------DEBUG: SSH command error: Traceback (most recent call last):
                                                             File "/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.venv_sic/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sic_framework/devices/alphamini.py", line 13, in <module>
                                                             from sic_framework.devices.common_mini.mini_animation import MiniAnimation, MiniAnimationActuator
                                                             File "/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.venv_sic/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sic_framework/devices/__init__.py", line 2, in <module>
                                                             from .pepper import Pepper
                                                             File "/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.venv_sic/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sic_framework/devices/pepper.py", line 7, in <module>
                                                             from pkg_resources import DistributionNotFound, get_distribution
                                                             ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'
                                                             Exception ignored in atexit callback: <function cleanup_on_exit at 0x79f31f6340>
                                                             Traceback (most recent call last):
                                                             File "/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.venv_sic/lib/python3.12/site-packages/

```
The nao/pepper package-level imports in `devices/__init__.py` breaks when running `devices/alphamini.py` because `pkg_resources` (which is part of the setuptools package) is not found. The dependencies for alphamini are installed manually, which means they are not installed via `install_requires` because the --no-deps flag is passed to avoid unnecessary installations like `opencv-python`.

## What is the new behavior?
For a quick fix, we moved the `pkg_resources` import inside a function in `pepper.py` to avoid the dependency at the module level.


## Other information

We should consider using absolute imports (e.g., from sic_framework.devices.nao import Nao) and remove importing the nao and pepper classes in `devices/__init__.py` to avoid loading unnecessary dependencies between devices. Although this reduces the simplicity of imports for users, it results in a cleaner design. We also need to clean up `install_requires` in `setup.py` to separate the absolute core dependencies from device-dependent/demo-dependent ones—for example, `opencv-python` is quite heavy and unnecessary if you are not running any camera demos. 

This issue has been addressed in #59

## Description

This pull request updates the default branch protection rules for the `project-links` repository. The main change involves standardizing the naming conventions for required status checks and adding a new validation step.

Updates to branch protection rules:

Specifically, updated "Check GitHub Actions with zizmor," "Check Justfile Format," and "Check Markdown links" to their prefixed versions.
* [`stack/project-links.tf`](diffhunk://#diff-8d4a200df5e9c4325ae12ffba43bb709aed7403c35680e7b6b89e058fa1f37aeL61-R67): Added a new required status check, "Common Code Checks / Lefthook Validate," to enforce validation using Lefthook.

body: ## Description This PR adds a Sign Up button to the Nav bar - Clerk Sign up button in the nav bar wrapping an OakSecondary Button, only visible to signed out teachers - Redirects to Onboarding after sign up - Redirects back to start point after Onboarding Link to the designs - https://www.figma.com/design/YcWQMMhHPVVmc47cHHEEAl/Oak-Design-Kit?node-id=8866-10602&p=f&m=dev Link to the deployment https://deploy-preview-3421--oak-web-application.netlify.thenational.academy/ Closes [LESQ 1392- I want a Sign Up button in the Nav Bar](https://www.notion.so/oaknationalacademy/I-want-a-sign-in-button-in-the-nav-bar-1eb26cc4e1b180aca2e1cff136c5cef7) ## Issue(s) - The designs call for a font size of 14px and weight of 600, the closest design token I could find to that is "body-3-bold" which has a weight of 700 - There aren't tests for the redirects, I couldn't find any e2e tests at all actually. ## How to test Checking the button renders as expected 1. Go to the home page with a signed out account 2. You should see the sign up button 3. Click the Pupil link 4. The sign up button should disappear 5. Click the teacher link and sign up 6. After completing sign up you should see the use avatar instead of the sign up button Checking the redirects 1. Go to a page other than the home page in the Teacher user flow 2. Click the sign up button 7. Sign up with a new account 8. You should be redirected to onboarding after sign up is finished 9. Complete the onboarding 10. You should be redirected back to the page from step one after completing onboarding ## Screenshots How it used to look: How it should now look: ![Kapture 2025-05-20 at 16 51 45](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4630b81a-994e-4946-b75f-0839ffb5b409) ## Checklist - [x] Added or updated tests where appropriate - [ ] Manually tested across browsers / devices - [x] Considered impact on accessibility - [ ] Design sign-off - [ ] Approved by product owner - [ ] Does this PR update a package with a breaking change

author: kartographer
body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->
First numba-based refactor.

## Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
Integrates numba, replaces the baseline utils originally developed in Cython.

## Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. If this PR closes an issue, put the word 'closes' before the issue link to auto-close the issue when the PR is merged. -->

This PR is meant to be a "first pass" at refactoring some of the old cython code using numba, integrating some work that @mkolopanis and I did while exploring if we could get the numba-based routines to perform as quickly as the cython-based ones. Since they were relatively straightforward to test and translate, we focused on the `utils.bls` module first. I'm attaching a notebook that @mkolopanis primarily put together for testing -- the good news is that I think I've got the numba versions of routines actually working at close to parity with the cython code (and for large-N, actually running _better_ than cython). Note that the inputs for the numba routines are slightly different, in that I've slightly refactored the higher level utils to be a bit smarter (e.g., finding the min/max values once, using those for both input-checking and choosing the cipher), so for fairness I've run timing tests with and without this "optimized overhead".

Note that for the moment, I haven't deleted the old cython routines, although they are no longer being used by any of the existing code at the moment.

Closes #1544

author: maxymnaumchyk
body:
Taking the restrictions of Virtual Array generator into account (that it has to return a `NumpyArray`) I've broken the `nestedindex` function into smaller pieces to construct final array's **content**, **offsets** and **parameters** separately. 

`_nestedindex` is a function for eager case

`_nestedindex_content` returns **content** as soon as it constructs it

`_get_nested_index_offsets` constructs **offsets** from the **content**

`_combine_parameters` combines **parameters** of index[0] and index[1]

And this whole thing does work. However I wonder if there is a simpler way to do this, without creating separate functions for virtual arrays construction. Is there maybe a way to have only one `lambda` function that would return **content** array, **offsets** array and **parameters** all at once?
